text_fidelity_a:
myCharge PowerGear Sound Protective Portable Charging Case for Wireless Earbuds Headphones | Custom Tray Compatible with Powerbeats & Removable for Other Brands | 1400 mAh / 1A Output The MyCharge is a handy if not tiny clamshell charging case for PowerBeat headphones, though it will work for others as well.

Pros:
The case itself has an hard outer shell that feels durable and thick. I have no fears the earbuds will be well protected inside. It opens and closes easily and tightly. As much as a case can be, it’s aesthetically pleasing—a dark, slick black with a black ribbon with red stitching running down the middle (the red stitching matches the red inside). The ribbon/band does more than add a bit of style and color; it also gives it a bit more texture so it grips the surface it’s atop better.

The plastic tray inside is designed for the PoweBeats line, so the earbuds nestle snugly (but with no need to wrestle or force them in) into an indentation so they lie flat and with a mid-section to insert the connecting wires/controls into. It’s a good fit, well-designed, and I don’t feel like I’m overstressing the wires, though I wouldn’t want to leave them in that position for a long amount of time (though I tend to worry about that sort of thin more than others)

It comes with a cable. You can use any one, but you’ll want it to be very short

The port to charge the case (the battery inside the case for sticklers) is easily accessible.

An LED on the front lets you know if the case battery is getting low

Cons
I wish the port cover felt a little more durable

Mixed or Up in the Air
I haven’t had it long enough yet to check how many charges, but I’ve gotten a few without a noticeable impact on the case battery. I don’t know if their promise of a dozen-plus will bear out, but I don’t think it’ll be far off if not.

The case isn’t really tiny (You can see the dimensions above). If you’re looking for something to slip into a pocket, then this will be a con, though it will easily fit a coat pocket. It will fit cargo pockets but you’ll definitely know it’s there. On the other hand, it doesn’t take up a lot of space, it’s quite protective, and if you’re worried about losing your expensive but very small and easy to lose earbuds, putting them in a noticeable, protective case that will also charge them back up is far from the worst idea. Personally, I’m OK with the size.

As noted, the case is designed for PowerBeats, so your mileage will vary on how well it fits some other type. My other earbuds all fits in the case without an issue, just not as snugly or neatly. That isn’t a real priority for me even ignoring the fact that I have PowerBeats.

Overall, a good value for what it does I’d say.
text_fidelity_b: myCharge PowerGear Sound Protective Portable Charging Case for Wireless Earbuds Headphones | Custom Tray Compatible with Powerbeats & Removable for Other Brands | 1400 mAh / 1A Output

HP Chromebook 14 Laptop, Intel Celeron N4000 Processor, 4 GB RAM, 32 GB eMMC, 14” HD Display, Chrome, Lightweight Computer with Webcam and Dual Mics, Home, School, Music, Movies (14a-na0021nr, 2021) After using my MacBook Pro all day, I always have a short adjustment period when I pick up a Chromebook. Compared to a normal Mac or Windows laptop, a Chromebook is very basic, very slimmed down on what it can do. Basically, ChromeOS is like turning an Android phone or tablet into a computer. ChromeOS runs on Google: Google Play for apps, games, books, etc., Google Drive for word processing, spreadsheets, etc., Gmail for email, Chrome for web browsing, and so on.

I know schools use Chromebooks but I don’t have kids, so my review is from the perspective of someone who uses a Chromebook for light browsing and streaming. For that purpose, it’s good.

The battery on this HP Chromebook lasts about 10 hours for watching shows and movies. I like that I can just grab it, watch for a few hours, and only have to remember to charge it a few times a week. Unlike some other Chromebooks, this one has only the standard laptop form factor, it doesn’t tent or fold. It also doesn’t have a touchscreen, which can be frustrating when trying to use Google Play apps on it.

The display is just okay, not very bright compared to my MacBook Pro, but then, that’s an unfair comparison to make. The sound quality (Bang & Olufsen audio) is good, making up for the display. The keyboard is not backlit and is missing some keys, like Caps Lock for a Search button.

The screen of the Chromebook has a black plastic edge that sticks out slightly from the white shell of the lid. I’m pretty gentle and careful with electronics, but I notice the black plastic edge pressing back into the white shell whenever I open the laptop. This is right where the webcam is. I’m worried that overtime, this area could break, since it’s already giving a little and I’ve only had the Chromebook for a few weeks.

The Chromebook charges via USB-C. It has two USB-C ports, one on either side, one USB-A port, an audio port, and an SD card slot. It has Bluetooth and WiFi; without an internet connection, a Chromebook is almost useless.
text_fidelity_b: HP Chromebook 14 Laptop, Intel Celeron N4000 Processor, 4 GB RAM, 32 GB eMMC, 14” HD Display, Chrome, Lightweight Computer with Webcam and Dual Mics, Home, School, Music, Movies (14a-na0021nr, 2021)

The best description I can offer of the sound quality is “clean.” The upper and mid ranges come through very clearly and are far more well-defined than typical with budget/value earbuds. The bass is not pronounced. It’s there, but it’s not what I’d describe as punchy. These are not an ideal set if you’re looking for head-thumping bass.

The comfort is typical for Brainwavz, which is to say it’s excellent. There’s a variety of ear tips so you can customize the fit to your ear. I’m especially fond of the Comply foam tips since they provide a great (but still comfortable) seal. That helps maintain good sound isolation and also helps with the bass response. It also helps keep the earbuds in place while exercising.

The cords are thin but seem sturdy enough for typical use. The same for the ear buds themselves. While they don’t have as solid of a build quality as higher-priced models, I don’t get the feeling that these will be falling apart anytime soon. That being said, it would have been nice to have more reinforcement where the cord meets the earbud, since that’s a prime stress point in use (even though these come with a very well made carry case, more often than not I just wind them around whatever device I am using).

For the price these are hard to beat. Highly recommend these as a not too expensive way to substantially upgrade from the stock earbuds that come with many devices.
[Sample provided for review]

text_fidelity_a:
Bluetooth Headphones, Soundcore Spirit Sports Earbuds by Anker, Bluetooth 5.0, 8H Battery, IPX7 Waterproof, SweatGuard, Comfortable Wireless Headphones, Secure Fit for Running, Gym, Workout These are around the same price as all the junky Chinese wireless earbud brands on Amazon but sound much better, are much more reliable, and are made by a company with good customer service that stands behind their products.

Ankers has several wireless earbuds with the cords that go behind the neck but only these, the spirit, the spirit pro, and the spirit x are worth considering for purchase. Their other earbuds are older models that cost just as much but have less features and weaker specs.

The bass on these is weak but I use these mostly for working out and for that it is fine.

I already have a pair of Apple EarPods but I wanted another wireless pair of headphones as well so I could switch back and forth while the other pair was charging.

These do not work with Apples w1 chip Bluetooth protocol, only apple and beats headphones work with that standard right now so those wireless headphones brands will sound better than anything other wireless headphones will with Apple products.

They also do not have aptx, which is the best sounding Bluetooth standard for anything other than Apple.

Ankers spirit pro headphones do support the aptx standard and supposedly have better bass than these so those are that models advantages.

However the spirit pro cost twice as much as these and only supports Bluetooth protocol 4.1 while these headphones support Bluetooth protocol 5.0.

Why is that important? Because the 5.0 protocol is the new “low energy” Bluetooth standard. Meaning that if you have both a device and headphones that support it you will get much more play time out of the same size battery.

Ankers other most recent model of earbuds, the spirit x headphones, have the same specs as these headphones in terms of the protocols they support but have a different form factor, obviously, and have 10mm drivers while these have 6mm. They also have a little more battery life.

I think I might buy the spirit x headphones as well in order to have a backup and to compare their sound.

As an Apple user the spirit pro headphones are just not worth the extra cost for me since I will never use the aptx protocol and they do not even support the Bluetooth 5.0 protocol.
If they were Bluetooth 5.0 compatible I might consider spending the extra 25 bucks in order to get that extra bass.

While these don’t sound spectacular they will get great battery life when I use them with devices that support 5.0 Bluetooth and they are very affordable.

I want to quickly rant about amazons policies and the flood of cheap Chinese products on here.

If you search for “wireless earbuds” or “Bluetooth earbuds” or any similar terms ankers products will not even show up on the first several pages of results.
Nor will Aukeys headphones, which I think are the second best option for wireless headphones in this price range.

Why is this?
Because the Chinese brands pay “click farms” to leave hundreds or even thousands of 5 star reviews.

The fraud is so obvious. What do you think is happening when a product has more than a thousand 5 star reviews all left on the same day or within the same few days and almost none of those reviews are from verified buyers?
The fact that many of them say the same things over and over and that many of them are written in broken English are other obvious clues.

I reported a few of them but Amazon does not take them down because Amazon cares about money and absolutely nothing else and having millions of people purchase this Chinese junk off their website makes them a lot of money.

It really sucks because good products, like these anker headphones, are barely visible in amazon search results because reputable brands don’t pay click farms to manipulate amazon search results.

It’s the consumers that lose in the end when their headphones, or other cheap Chinese products, break a few weeks after use or maybe never even work to begin with.
And you can bet that half of the time the companies selling this junk on amazon will simply disappear in order to avoid accepting returns and then reappear later under a new seller account to sell more junk through click farm manipulated amazon search results.

Of course amazon will find itself on the hook for some of these costs but apparently the money they make off of allowing all of this Chinese junk to be sold on their website under false practices is much more than any costs they incur.

These practices that amazon allows, and this one issue about manipulated search results is just the tip of the iceberg, hurts not just American consumers it also hurts American companies.

Rant over.
text_fidelity_b: Bluetooth Headphones, Soundcore Spirit Sports Earbuds by Anker, Bluetooth 5.0, 8H Battery, IPX7 Waterproof, SweatGuard, Comfortable Wireless Headphones, Secure Fit for Running, Gym, Workout

Avantree DG40SA Dedicated Windows 10 Bluetooth USB Adapter, Wireless Dongle for PC Bought with Win 10, Plug & Play, Support Headpones, PS4 Gaming Controllers, Mouse, Keyboard, Printers etc. I purchased a Lenovo Ideacentre AIO Y910 in December 2017 and it had a beautiful built-in Qualcomm bluetooth function. It worked great. I had my desktop paired with my Echo Dots and with Alexa could continue listening to movies/music/podcasts/youtube anywhere in my house away from the computer. Along came a Windows 10 update in March 2018 that disabled/removed the bluetooth function/drivers ENTIRELY. No roll backs/restores, or reinstallations brought it back. The internal bluetooth function was completely ruined and prevented from running. I was furious and microsoft support was zero help. I finally begrudgingly purchased this to do the same function. I'm angry I had to pay for something I already paid for my computer to have, and that I have to waste a USB spot for it, but it works, was truly plug and play, though the connecting of all my speakers/Echo Dots is more complicated that previously. For example, with the original bluetooth capabilities, I could chose to have one or both of the Dots automatically connect when bluetooth was enabled. I could have them play together or verbally tell Alexa to connect/disconnect. Now for some reason with this bluetooth, voice control doesn't work, Alexa can't disconnect (she will do it but then it automatically reconnects) and if one Dot is connected the other won't. I have to run back to my computer's bluetooth settings and pair/unpair and connect/disconnect each time I want to make a change. This is frustrating. If anyone knows of anyway to circumvent this or the original bluetooth death please let me know, I'd be forever grateful.

The range for the device is fine, I live in a 1200 sq ft two story townhome and there was no issue with my computer seeing the Dot in the bedroom or the Dot downstairs. Connections are strong.

text_fidelity_a:
Seagate Momentus XT 750 GB 7200RPM SATA 6Gb/s 32 MB Cache 2.5 Inch Solid State Hybrid Drive ST750LX003 This drive is not that fast and it freezes the computer too. Copying files to this drive would get the same speed from any drive that is either SATA 3G, SATA 6G or even from a SATA adapter card. Imagine 5400 16mb on IDE speed. And let me tell you about installation of Adobe Master Collection CS5.5 after a clean OS installation. It would stop, freeze and even give an error message or two. Installing Adobe to other regular SATA drives is fine. It isn't just Adobe either. I don't think this drive is meant to be run as your Operating System if it freezes all the time like this and give this kind or read and write speed. My bios is set to AHCI for the SATA controller and running on the Intel driver for the IDE ATA/ATAPI controller so it isn't my computer that is causing the problems I just mentioned. Formatting the drive was easy. You can just use the latest Maxtor MaxBlast 5 and it will format fine. In fact they suggested that on their own website for formatting and cloning.

This drive is going back this week as soon as I can clone the ISO onto another drive so that I don't have to reinstall everything. This is a great shame because I had great hope for this product. But then again Seagate has never been my favorite company for hard drives.

P.S. I installed this on a desktop with BOXDH67BLB3 motherboard, a 2600k CPU and 16 gb of RAM. The hard drive was connected directly to a SATA 6G port on the motherboard which showed no sign of the kind of speed I was expecting from the spec this drive supposed to have.
text_fidelity_b: Seagate Momentus XT 750 GB 7200RPM SATA 6Gb/s 32 MB Cache 2.5 Inch Solid State Hybrid Drive ST750LX003

text_fidelity_a:
Ultimate Ears MEGABOOM 3 Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker (Powerful Sound + Thundering Bass, Bluetooth, Magic Button, Waterproof, Battery 20 hours) - Lagoon Blue I used to be a big Ultimate Ears guy from the aughts before they were bought by Logitech who killed their best product lines and replaced it with stuff like... THIS. The tiresome photos of impossibly gleeful adult-babies listening to music underwater and having the times of their lives thanks to this f——g speaker really gets cloying when it’s printed on literally everything except the device itself. But that’s Logitech for you. Of all things I have to complain about with this speaker, the sound isn’t one of them. Unlike its predecessors and smaller cousins, the Megaboom 3 doesn’t peak out the bass quite so much when it would otherwise be distorted. (This is the most common bit of digital audio gimmickry to fool you into think it sounds “crystal clear”.) The people complaining about this speaker in these reviews who say other brands are better are just brands more notorious for “loudness fakery” to make the sound seem more bass-heavy but is really just slick audio post-processing. It’s makes hip hop sound a little better but everything else is a murky mess. But I digress. This speaker does all of the digital trickery, sure, but at least the actual amplifier and speaker drivers aren’t rubbish so that’s I plus. I was playing System of a Down cranked in my bedroom and it sounded amazing, especially compared to my former Boom speaker which someone nicked from my garage. Where the Boo crumpled trying to product screeching highs and thumping lows the Megaboom 3 dominated. Of course I don’t use any of the EQ tomfoolery and let it play as close to how the music was engineered to play and its just dandy. Okay then, good sound: check.
The problem with this speaker, like all of the other UE speakers, is the brain-dead user interface and obnoxious audio feedback that you can’t properly adjust without hacking the device configs (allegedly). There is literally a single on/off switch for all audio feedback. Wut? No relative volume of system sounds compared to music, or selection of which sounds you want to hear and which ones you don’t, like that HORRIBLY OBNOXIOUS LOUD BEEP it makes that’s louder than the music if you accidentally lean in on your volume up button? Of course every sound is as loud as or louder than the music your playing. That’s just great. Furthermore, if you are listening to music through your iPad or iPhone, it decides to insert little beeps for certain feedback notifications that never happen when you are just using your device without the speaker. It’s horribly distracting and unnecessary, but worse is that you NEED audio feedback on if you want to be able to Bluetooth connect to it as audio feedback is the only feedback you get.

Ugh. Sorry, had a bit of a rant there.

It’s tough because I think the speak sounds decent and almost worth the price, but the UI team at Logite... excuse me... Ultimate Ears are clearly huffing paint fumes as each product they subsequently release is even more unpleasant to use than the last. Don’t let the coked-out looking teens with bright, expensive clothing printed on the box fool you.

text_fidelity_a:
(OLD MODEL) Seagate Expansion 3TB Desktop External Hard Drive USB 3.0 (STBV3000100) So far, the hard drive is working as one would expect. As always with these things, the questions mostly arise in longevity/reliability issues, so I'll be updating this once I've had a longer time to determine how it does in those categories. First impressions at this point, though:

1) the drive has a relatively small footprint, which is nice

2) Feels quite sturdy and hefty (it's surprisingly heavy) with good build quality

3) This isn't powered by your USB, so you'll need an outlet for its enclosed power cord

4) When you start up, it takes a little while (a few seconds) for the display light to come on. At first, I thought it hadn't started up at all, but just wait a small bit and it will light up

5) the display light is located on top but at the rear of the device, which while minor, is a slight inconvenience. I have it under my desk set back a little ways, so to see the light isn't as immediate as one might like

6) the drive is quite quiet. Not silent--you can hear it--but definitely quieter than many I've had

7) the drive is pretty fast, with the uptick from USB 2 to 3 very noticeable as I move from one computer (USB 2) to the other (USB 3)--it varies depending on what I'm copying, but sometimes the difference is half the speed

8) despite the small footprint, with its necessity for power and it's weight, I wouldn't consider this at all a portable drive, though I suppose you could use it as such. But really, it's big and heavy for that.

9) I use this on several Macs--no problem at all reformatting it for those computers--just a few mouse clicks and a few seconds is all

So far, this is a good big backup drive (I have the 5 TB version). And since we all know, or should, that drives will fail, you can't have too many of them. If any issues arise over time, I'll update accordingly
text_fidelity_b: (OLD MODEL) Seagate Expansion 3TB Desktop External Hard Drive USB 3.0 (STBV3000100)

Echo Plus with built-in Hub 1st Generation – Black [please see update below original review]

I bought the original Echo when it was first available for pre-order and have loved it. No issues. The opposite is the case with Echo Plus.

Doesn't understand me half the time.
Intermittent success using the remote.
Tried multiple times setting up groups to play music simultaneously in different rooms using it with my 2 echo dots and original Echo. Echo Plus responds by doing nothing, or playing a random song or stations, and nothing on the other units in the group.

I really hate returning things, but unless there are fixes in updates between now and the end of the return period, that's what I'll be doing. Seriously disappointed. Oh, and I called Amazon "help" so-called, and I knew more about how it works than the person I wasted 15 minutes on the phone with. It was a surreal convo.
= = =
UPDATE: This morning I got a call from Anthony, from Amazon customer service. First, I was blown away that they would call me to address my issues with Echo Plus. Second, he was knowledgeable, and in no hurry. While it remains to be seen whether every issue with EP is fixed, the problem with Groups was.

It turns out that Alexa didn't like the name I gave my group, it was that simple. My original Echo is black, my EP is white, so I called the group "Black And White". Suggestion: When setting up your groups, go with one of the suggested generic names--bedroom, living room, etc. Echo calls them "Common Names". I called mine "Backyard", even though my backyard isn't involved.

Regarding Alexa often not understanding me on the EP, Anthony suggested that I try switching from British english to American english. I'm going to try that, although I have used British english on my original Echo with no issues.

So, I've upgraded my review to 4 stars, and when and if all issues are resolved I'll be coming back to make it 5. Amazon support definitely gets 5 stars. Even though my first call was a disaster, the way they followed up was remarkable, and that's the important thing. Seriously impressed. Thank you, Anthony!

text_fidelity_a:
Perixx Periboard-512 Ergonomic Split Keyboard - Natural Ergonomic Design - Black - Bulky Size 19.09"x9.29"x1.73", US English Layout First let me tell you what I like about this keyboard: I like the key action. Keys have a decently long stroke and are easy to press and don't feel spongy. I like the split layout, which makes for a much more natural position for the arms. I like the split spacebar. To me, these are advantages over the Logitech K350 I've been using, which has a curved, not split, key layout and a spongy feel when typing.

What I don't like, and what was pretty much a dealbreaker to me (I thought about returning it almost immediately) is the "wrist rest." It is short and rolls off steeply and provides no wrist support at all, unless you like typing with your wrist positioned lower than your knuckles and your hands bent upwards from the wrist. The recommended position is wrist level with the knuckles, which is called the "neutral" position. I personally prefer typing with my wrists positioned slightly higher than my knuckles.

Look at the product photos and notice that the typist doesn't even have his wrist on the wrist rest. He or she is using a hover hand technique, I guess to make things look more ergonomic or something, because if their wrists were actually on the wrist rest, their hands would be obviously bent upwards at the wrists to reach the keys.

I'm at a loss as to why many keyboard manufacturers (including Logitech with the K350) provide legs to raise the back of the keyboard and don't provide anything to raise the front. That just makes the "backwards" bend at the wrist even more pronounced.

This Periboard keyboard is no exception to that. It has foldaway legs at the back and none in the front. But even if it had legs to raise the front, it wouldn't provide much improvement. I raised the front a couple of inches with a foam wedge I use for keyboard support, and the wrist rest was still so low I pressed the spacebar when reaching for the F2 key.

I even tried adding foam wrist rests but the built-in rest is so steep and short it actually interferes with using a really functional rest. I even tried using wearable wrist rests---which are kind of annoying on their own since they aren't all that stable---and the steep slope and short length of the built-in wrist rest made that a less than effective solution. This keyboard might have been a lot better if it had no built-in wrist rest at all. That way you could use your own and set it up just like you like it.

It's disappointing, actually. I like the key action and layout, but the wrist rest pretty much nerfs the whole thing. I may keep it and experiment with solutions from time to time. I might even see if I can cut off the built-in rest and replace it with something made of wood or something, or just get it out of the way so I can use some other effective wrist rest.

In the meantime, I'm probably going to stick with the spongy-action, non-split Logitech K350. In fact I'm typing this review on it, though I would have liked to use the Periboard 512. But until I come up with a better wrist rest solution it's just easier to use the K350.

And a couple more quick points, comparing this keyboard to the K350, this keyboard is wired while the K350 is wireless. The overall footprint of both (length and width) is almost the same. I personally don't use or need the multimedia keys on either.

Because of the better key action and, to me, better key layout, if it had a better wrist rest, or none at all, this Periboard 512 might have become my go-to keyboard.
text_fidelity_b: Perixx Periboard-512 Ergonomic Split Keyboard - Natural Ergonomic Design - Black - Bulky Size 19.09"x9.29"x1.73", US English Layout

LotFancy Laptop Cooler Cooling Pad with 5 Quiet Fans for 12-17" Notebook, Dual USB Ports Disclaimer: I was sent this product to evaluate so that I could write an informed review.

Actually this is my second LotFancy cooling pad, and I took it because I do like their products. I haven't had any bad experiences with them except for breaking off one of the little plastic stops that keeps your laptop from sliding off the pad when the rear is elevated, but that was entirely my fault. I left the pad on the floor and someone stepped on it. Can't blame LotFancy for that.

The design of this pad is kind of interesting. It has two controls, one for the large center fan and the other for the four smaller side fans. This, plus the width of the pad itself, allows you to use various sizes of laptop efficiently. If you have a small one, you never need to turn on the side fans. If you have a 17" one, they're in position to help you cool it. I'm curious as to why the green light (signaling that the center fan is on) is set so much lower than the light for the side banks. A strange feature, though not something I have a problem with. It's just odd.

The pad is adjustable to seven different heights (including flat), so you've got a lot of positions to choose from. I write in a variety of places around the house, so this is one of my favorite things about the pad. It allows me to work without having to find all sorts of things to prop my laptop on. The locking mechanism is solid. Since it's USB-powered, there's an extra USB port at the back so that you don't lose that functionality. Most cooling pads have some way of doing this, so it's expected rather than special. It's quiet, but it's far from super silent.

It's a good pad. Yes, some of the construction seems a bit flimsy, but my other LotFancy pad has held together just fine and I see no reason to think this one won't.

text_fidelity_a:
Jabra Evolve 65t True Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds, UC Optimized – Superior Call Quality and Connectivity – Passive Noise Cancelling Earbuds with up to 15 hours of Battery Life with Charging Case When reviewing headsets, I don't just pop them on and hit play on a favorite song or take a call. I actually run them through a battery of sound tests from an audio site. I run all sets through the same test to make it fair. First on my PC and then on my iPhone XS. I find it's the best way to make an unbiased review.
• Bass: Poor with a limited range. It also wasn’t balanced between the earbuds.
• High freq: Better than the bass, but still a limited range. It was balanced between the earbuds much better though.
• Rattle: None, but it would be weird if earbuds rattled. Ok that’s not true, I stepped on a pair at the gym that rattled afterwards. Oops.
• Volume: Sufficient. I don’t blast my earbuds, because I like to keep my hearing. I could turn it low enough to not hear, and loud enough to be uncomfortable.
• Clarity: Isolated for the sound test they did fine. However, outside the site the clarity started to degrade, and on a call was bad enough to be an issue.

The sound check results were mediocre. Bass was lacking, as was the general range of the set. These actually did worse than their cheaper behind the neck set (Jabra Evolve 65e UC).

As for things other than sound, like usability I like to ask myself what I’m looking for and if product meets those expectations. So, here goes:

Would these last the entire workday?
Yes and No, if you take them off to charge during lunch then you will probably be fine. Otherwise no they are going to die out about 75% through a standard 8 hr workday. They require a USB port and their little case thing to charge. I had no issues as long as I remember to charge them at lunch.

Are they easy to use?
The basics, yes. All the extra features, not so much. I opened the box up and was happy to see the quick-start guide, unfortunately if there is a manual I didn't get one. I found a digital copy tucked away in the iPhone app, but nothing in the box itself. That made anything past the basics in the quick-start guide a matter of trial and error, until I found the manual tucked away in the App. For the price, that seems like a rather cheap move. There is a ton of useful info in the manual that is not contained in the quick-start guide.

Can I take calls seamlessly?
Yes, but for me at least the call experience was lacking. The voices on some but not all calls were a bit muddled, however they could hear me just fine. So poor marks for the sound quality, but high marks for the mic.
Speaking of mics, can I mute the mic easily?
Easily, yes. But knowing for sure if you are muted (we've all been there) only when using the computer dongle, on my iPhone using Bluetooth, eek not so much. Had to leave it to faith. That was a bit scary.

Plays music well (aka does it have range and bass)?
Meh. I have the sound review at the top. As you can imagine, lack of bass negatively impacts listening to music. I mean it wasn’t awful but it wasn’t great either.

Can I opt to hear people talking to me (audio pass-through)?
Yes, but it sounds super static and buzzy. The sound is not clear and crisp at all. Also, you can't just pop an earbud out and listen with one ear. If the earbuds are anymore than head-width apart they stop working all together. According to the manual, you should be able to use the right earbud by itself, but that was not my experience. It also would stop working (although it worked a bit longer than the left) once they were too far apart.

Noise-canceling abilities, can I at least block out the cubical next to me?
Sort of. You can block drumming blah blah blah sounds, but ringing phones and coworkers talking, not so much. Although it did take the edge off. The Jabra iPhone app for these has some cool ambient sound machine settings, waves crashing, thunderstorm, white noise, etc. Probably my favorite thing about this whole set.

Are they comfortable?
I didn't like them, but I am a petite human and have small ears. I also don't like the weird vacuuming pressure you feel when wearing anything noise-cancelling. I will give these neutral marks for comfort, I think if you had larger ear canals and didn't mind closed type headsets these would probably be fine.

Are these worth the price?
Nope. For the price these should be spectacular and check all the boxes. They are mediocre in sound quality even though they are packed with features. If you plan on just tossing them on and not actually testing the audio, go for it. They work. But for the price, they should handle music and calls equally well. They do not.

Overall, I will have to say I was rather disappointed with these. I also reviewed their behind the neck version (Jabra Evolve 65e UC) and was hoping I had just gotten a dud with that set. Well lightening either struck twice, or the audio on these is even worse than the cheaper behind the neck version. Darn, because I wanted to love these. I have a soft spot for gadgets with cool features. These had potential. I will give them three stars because if the price point wasn’t so high, they would be okay. Not great, but they’d get the job done. I also really liked the ambient sounds you could listen to on the app. A nice little extra that was unexpected.

Hope that helps!
text_fidelity_b: Jabra Evolve 65t True Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds, UC Optimized – Superior Call Quality and Connectivity – Passive Noise Cancelling Earbuds with up to 15 hours of Battery Life with Charging Case

With it, I can easily verify whether a given charger is actually outputting the advertised power. So far I've tried it on an Anker 65W charger and an Apple 96W charger connected to a MacBook Pro and both times the cable LED agreed with the charger's ratings. This cable will come in handy when I occasionally need to charge with strange/no-name chargers or built-in USB plugs at some hotels.

The cable is pretty long - 10' as the product description indicates - and also a bit stiffer than I expected. For now I feel uncomfortable wrapping it around my hand into a ring as I usually do with cables, especially since the cable came folded and it's hard to get rid of the creases. Included on the cable is a velcro strap that makes keeping things tidy either way.

I think this is a very useful cable - especially the addition of the LED will make it a companion in my travels. I recommend it.

It's of good weight, easy to adjust, two lens for viewing through eyes or phone, came with some sample specimens to look at and a manual that there's a lot of reading. Specimens are in glass like how you used to get in the lab, also came with blank ones that you can make your own (like swabbing your mouth). First off you do have to check all the lenses because they can be loose. Mine were and I caught it, glad nothing broke. I personally didn't feel it easy to understand the instructions so I'd say it's better if you have experience in the past (or YouTube) so touching a delicate equipment like this isn't as intimidating. Now I couldn't get the cell phone feature to work. It uses suction cups and my phone keeps sliding down with gravity. When I try to look with my phone it's the best I could get(in the picture) . Because of that I say this microscope failed my cell phone test, but everything else works as described.
text_fidelity_b: Vanstarry Beginners Microscope Kit 40X-1000X for Kids & Students, Dual LED Lights and Cordless Capability, Illumination Lab Compound Monocular Microscopes with Optical Glass Lenses & 12 Slides

text_fidelity_a:
OTTERBOX DEFENDER SERIES Case for iPad mini (5th Gen ONLY) - Retail Packaging - BLACK So. Yes. It’s sturdy and seems it’ll protect an iPad really well.

Unfortunately, for the past 6 years, we’ve been spoiled by an iPad mini case made by Ballistic, that isn’t made any more. So I just don’t buy “well sure it’s inconvenient and bulky but it has to be, to protect well.” It really does not.

This plastic Otterbox uses is so very rigid, the protective cover is extremely difficult to pop on and off. When kiddo’s alarm goes off and he’s already off somewhere, it takes me ages to get the thing open to shut it down. I also can’t find the power or volume buttons easily by touch, they blend in so much.

What’s outright laughable is the kickstand. It’s on the inside of the cover that you take off, so you set the iPad on it. It doesn’t sit very securely at all, and now that this model has the pencil holder, in some positions it won’t stay up - it teeter totters right over! So no, it’s not a 4 position kickstand, but a 3 position. The whole situation is anything but stable, so if there’s a tug on a charger or headphone cord, instead of just sliding a tiny bit on the table or not doing anything at all, it slips off the kickstand and ... well, this is how we already know it’s sturdy, as the thing ended up on the floor more times in the first day than the iPad did in a year in its old case.

It’s quite heavy compared to other choices that offer similar protection, and very very difficult to install. I am never need to read directions type, and these directions were meaningless. It required a YouTube and a lot of swearing, plus a sliced open cuticle, to get it on. Even then it didn’t seat properly around the speakers and needed quite a bit of poking into place with a toothpick.

I sincerely hope there will be a day when there’s another rugged iPad mini case, with a kickstand and a shell that goes over the screen. Because this just doesn’t cut it.
text_fidelity_b: OTTERBOX DEFENDER SERIES Case for iPad mini (5th Gen ONLY) - Retail Packaging - BLACK

text_fidelity_a:
Gosky 12x55 High Definition Monocular Telescope and Quick Smartphone Holder - 2018 This is a really nice optical device. I hadn't necessarily heard of Gosky before, but I gather they are a big brand in optics. I'm also going on relatively little education on the subject that a monocular is easier to focus at longer distances and/or a larger range of distances because you don't have to focus the two lenses - something which makes it hard for me to look through binoculars after a while.

This is pretty lightweight, but feels very solid and nice. It has a turn-out piece to the rear of the rear lens to accommodate people who don't wear glasses. And besides that, there is only one knob to turn to focus, mostly depending on the distance to the object of your attention.

The carry case is fairly rugged nylon and has a belt loop, but not the kind of belt loop you can use without unstrapping your belt. It's also a little large for a belt in my opinion, but may come in handy. The hand strap is pretty nice, but there is a lot of extra length to the strap I really don't know what to do with, and I feel like the actual attachment process could be more refined. I do really like that both lens covers can stay attached to the body while not in use (rear one can be attached to the hand strap and front on is attached to a rubber ring which stays on the body) which makes for a refined and complete product.

Not sure if this one can accommodate a cell phone holder or not...seems like people must take pictures through these things when birding or spying or watching opera or whatever they're doing.

Nice product. I now have a good feeling about this brand that was previously off my radar.
text_fidelity_b: Gosky 12x55 High Definition Monocular Telescope and Quick Smartphone Holder - 2018

Sony ZX Series Wired On-Ear Headphones with Mic, White MDR-ZX110AP I certainly didn't expect anything of audiophile quality or anything astounding. Knowing how much I'm spending is the context for the review.

It's a good pair of headphones.

They're lightweight, comfortable, the earpads stay reasonably cool, the cord is just long enough to listen to at a desk (and that's a good thing), and they sound awfully good for what I paid. They also look pretty okay. The fact that they fold flat is a nice little bonus but for a pair of utility headphones, I think these are a home run.

So as a sound engineer and a musician I would put it this way. They're not high fidelity headphones, nor do they work for performance. They won't work for reference/studio work at all. They're too flimsy to call a solid pair, but for casually listening to music while multi-tasking at home or for watching a streaming video, these do just great. I think there are a number of good headphones like this one you can get for less than $20 or so. This one is up there and I would buy it again if I needed another.

text_fidelity_a: Amazon Fire TV - 1st Generation I love this thing. I've had it a couple of weeks, and I am still exploring. We did have one problem with it. Yesterday it stopped streaming videos. Just came up and either said player error or another message telling us to clear all data in the settings. I know I had lost my internet connection, but it wasn't as easy as just resetting my modem. We fiddled and fiddled and did what it said, after reconnecting the internet we had to clear the data. This fixed it , and it is now working perfectly again. My only complaint is that troubleshooting information was hard to find. Even the error messages were not easy to understand. In spite of that, if it had needed to be replaced, I would have been counting the days. I love this thing. It's sooooooooooooo wonderful to be able to watch movies and TV series without commercials. The picture is crystal clear and it's really easy to use. The voice search works extremely well. There are tons of free shows to watch, and free good music as well that you can play on your other devices free of charge. I will gladly renew my Prime subscription, even if I do have to pay for a movie once in a while. Also note, jaded Directv users- Amazon charges much less to watch a new movie. If I could get Fox News on it, I'd cancel Directv.  I am extremely happy with this purchase, even with the little problem.

WiFi Video Projector, WEWATCH V10B Wireless Portable Movie Projector with Bluetooth Full HD 1080P Supported Home Theater Video Projector Compatible with HDMI, VGA, TV Stick, iPhone, Android The WEWATCH V30 Portable Projector is a good 1080p projector for its size. I watched some movies with the screen setup to 80-90 inches and the picture looked very good in a dark room. It's important to watch this projector in low ambient lighting due to its low ANSI lumens, as bright light will wash out the picture.

The size of the projector is not as small as the pictures make it seem. Though it is not advertised as a pico projector, I expected it to be smaller. With that said, the projector is not so large that it would be hard to transport or store when not in use.

Unfortunately, I was not able to get the Wi-Fi feature to work with my Iphone. This is not a dealbreaker for me, as I plugged a Roku stick into the HDMI port and the system worked well.

I was surprised by how good the native speakers sound. I found watching movies enjoyable and voices were easy to hear. There are adjustments for the bass and treble levels in the menus. The unit has a headphone jack in the rear which makes hooking up an external speaker set up a breeze.

The fan on the unit is very quiet and is not distracting while it is in use.

While I really like this projector, there is a large downside. The lack of keystone correction is a huge oversight. Placing this projector without keystone adjustment means the projector has to be directly in line with the viewing area making it necessary to use a tripod in most instances. Having to bring a tripod along, makes the unit less portable.

Overall, this is a small projector with a great picture, as long as you can place it in the perfect location without much ambient lighting. If WEWATCH added keystone correction and refined the mirroring feature, this would be a 5 star projector.
text_fidelity_b: WiFi Video Projector, WEWATCH V10B Wireless Portable Movie Projector with Bluetooth Full HD 1080P Supported Home Theater Video Projector Compatible with HDMI, VGA, TV Stick, iPhone, Android

I have the RainbowLight color, which is exactly what it says: a rainbow light strip.

The rainbow light stays the same when turned on, the light doesn’t pulse or fade or change to any other color. The light can be turned on or off, there is no dimmer option. The rainbow light is visible when using your laptop.

The fan works well. It’s quiet and effective. The fan has a wheel to adjust the speed.

The cooling pad is height adjustable. The “legs” have two sections that fit into each other to adjust the height/angle of the cooling pad. The two sections don’t lock into place which makes me paranoid, they just fit into each other. It’s sturdy once you get the cooling pad set up, but I wouldn’t leave my laptop on it if I wasn’t there to catch it in case of something happening.

If using the cooling pad at an angle, the baffle is needed to keep your laptop from sliding off. The baffle is a small rectangle of plastic that stores in a designated spot under the cooling pad. There are no other safeguards built into the cooling pad to hold a laptop in place, so if you lose that piece of plastic, you’re screwed. I have other similar fans that have small ridges or foam pieces for extra security.

text_fidelity_a:
Contour +2 - Old Packaging (Discontinued by Manufacturer) This is a really cool camera in a lot of ways, and yet there are two things about it that I hate:

1) It writes *.mov files. Why would any company choose that over so many great standards out there? Quicktime is the norm for *.mov files, with other players claiming to play them, but often with issues. Quicktime is one of those programs that - even after you uninstall it and delete everything you can find associated with it in your registry - will hound you until the end of your days to upgrade and constantly ask permission to take over your computer, will change other file extensions to play on it without asking, etc. Therefore, I so loathe Quicktime that I generally won't even touch an *.mov file.

I'd even be tempted to take the product down to three stars because of this, but there is some chance that this was the only format that would allow them to include the GPS data. I sort of doubt it because Apple (Quicktime) is the most ridiculously proprietary company I can think of, but I guess I need to give Contour the benefit of the doubt. Same benefit of the doubt used for annoyance #2:

2) You need to install more software to see the GPS data. I hate installing more and more software on my computer because everything installed is just another chance to have something running as a service or process all the time, wasting your resources. In general, all software is more "bloated" than ever these days, making our more powerful than before computers unable to perform better than before.

I also wish for some Blackberry support, but they might have some with BB OS 10, supposedly. Frankly, I'm not that interested in the smart phone features; they just slow you down.

As I said, the camera is really cool, though, for its ease of use and its mounts. It's obviously geared toward adventurers and people that want to roll off roofs in shopping carts like that one show that used to be popular. It has a great feel to it in its construction and durability, but I want to make clear the very big caveat that these are the only reasons you want this camera. Besides the annoyances mentioned above, I have a couple point and shoot cameras that do 1080p video just as well (actually better, given their native formats) and they are smaller and cost less. But it is pretty awesome to mount this on your bike for those "just in case" scenarios.
text_fidelity_b: Contour +2 - Old Packaging (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

This thang is FIYAH!!!!!!!!!!

Let's start with the unboxing: it arrives in a sleek, black box with a beautiful photo of the laptop on its cover, and when you open it, you are awed by the pristine, silver gleaming contraption inside. When you pick it up and gently unwrap it from its plastic film, you are wowed by how both light and elegant it is in your hands; how something so small can contain your life, and then you can't wait to start filling it up with it. You open the lid and lift the mesh cover protecting the keys; you notice the setup leaflet and take out the power cord, plug her in and turn her on.

From there, Cortana takes over, guiding you through the setup! By voice command! Very Jason Bourne. You set up your fingerprint log in, sign in to your accounts and then once everything is registered, off into the wild wild web you go. The first thing you'll notice is how FAST this baby is, the gentle whir of the machine as she takes you off to the farthest reaches of the world if you check out the 4K resolution by looking at the Planet Earth series. It's enough to bring tears to your eyes. You'll be mesmerized by the rhythmic clicking of the keys as you go to your favorite websites and download/install your must-have apps and programs; you will find yourself looking down at the keyboard and smiling as if you've been enchanted by a new lover, and you HAVE!

I had been looking for a new computer because I've got this ollllld slooooooooow, 4GB RAM dinosaur of an 15" laptop that I bought used in a dire emergency because I accidentally cracked the screen on my Toshiba. The "Gorilla glass" on this is so beautiful that I don't even want to TOUCH it, even though the touch screen is flawless, like you are on a tablet.

The keyboard is perfectly sized and responsive; there is just so much here for me to continue to explore but I am damn near breathless as I write this review because it is simply that exceptional, stunning. I have had some graphic design programs that I wanted to use but was waiting until I got something new so it would have the capacity to rock out, and I can't wait to get started. Where this HAS been incredible for me is Traktor and music programs. No more worrying about lag and staticky mixing because of system overload. This has all the memory and SSD space that you will need, and its ports will more than accommodate any other gadgets you need to connect to it. The sound is exemplary, with the Bang & Olufsen speakers.

This is the Ultrabook that every entrepreneur or very lucky student should have; it is the answer and perhaps even a juggernaut to the Macbook. I've certainly learned that just one POWERFUL Ultrabook is WORTH the investment rather than having to replace a tired ass notebook every few years. I prefer large screens so 13 inches has never appealed to me, but this right here has ROCKED. MY. WORLD. I don't wanna go anywhere without it, not even the shower. LOL

You have just got to see for yourself.

text_fidelity_a:
NETGEAR Orbi Compact Wall-Plug Whole Home Mesh WiFi System - WiFi router and wall-plug satellite extender with speeds up to 2.2 Gbps over 3,500 sq. feet, AC2200 (RBK20W) This is an updated version of a mesh system router and satellite I already have. The technology is great when it's working, but, for whatever reason, my system has needed to be reset once a week or more, and the coverage is nowhere near as good as it claims it should be.

My hope was that the newer version would be faster and have better coverage. It isn't. It doesn't. And, like the earlier version, it has to be in AP mode to work with my FIOS modem (FIOS has a version of this available with its own firmware, but you have to buy a new one, and it won't work with any other ISP). Those hopes dashed, my next hope was that I could at least use the router as a satellite on my existing system, which, of course not.

So, you would think I could at LEAST use the satellite from the new one with the old system or the old satellite with the new one? They are the same model, after all. And that, too, would be a nope.

What I finally did, after hours on the internet (and other hours just trying to set up the new one by itself - it was the same with the old one - it for some reason despises custom settings and will not save them the first many times. It will also lose them after firmware upgrades, I expect, like its predecessor), was set it up alongside the old one with its own network name. Now I have one network serving one side of the house and the other serving the other. Speeds are good. So far, no routing issues, and I don't really expect any. The two network solution seems to have worked well for others.

But really.

If you are looking to expand your Orbi network, check out the nighthawk mesh expanders. I have the 7500, and it's excellent. Also, don't take my lukewarm review for a no-rec. The Orbi is, as far as I can tell from personal experience, buggy and locked down, but, again from personal experience, it beats the Velop (its nearest competitor) by a mile for coverage.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR Orbi Compact Wall-Plug Whole Home Mesh WiFi System - WiFi router and wall-plug satellite extender with speeds up to 2.2 Gbps over 3,500 sq. feet, AC2200 (RBK20W)

text_fidelity_a:
Sony WF-1000XM4 Industry Leading Noise Canceling Truly Wireless Earbud Headphones with Alexa Built-in, Black This product feels different to me than other Sony stuff I've gotten. It's like they've gone out of their way to make everything feel like cardboard. The packaging was like egg carton, and the earbuds and their charging station are a rough lightweight material in a drab color. The earbuds themselves are customizable, but bulky compared to the competition. I find them hard to get out of the container, hard to hold onto, and hard to wear. The noise cancellation and sound are both above average though. I like the charging light on the container. It communicates with color and flashes what the status of the product is, and isn't bright or hard to locate.

USB-C charging makes the base station charge up nice and fast. It holds the earbuds securely, and doesn't rattle or fall open. It's also a nice pocketable size and shape with no sharp corners, making the whole product especially portable. Controls are gesture, rather than button. I'm not a fan of this because I end up doing a lot of swiping and hoping. A click button interface, I can just click it the number of times I know will do what I need, and move on.

I've got a few Sony audio products that I use every day and am very happy with, but with earbuds, I'm sticking with jabra for now. It's a competitive market right now for earbuds. Lots of companies putting out new designs.
text_fidelity_b: Sony WF-1000XM4 Industry Leading Noise Canceling Truly Wireless Earbud Headphones with Alexa Built-in, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Polk Audio Atrium 6 Outdoor Speakers with Bass Reflex Enclosure (Pair, Black) - All-Weather Durability | Broad Sound Coverage | Speed-Lock Mounting System The Good:
-They sound good. They're not audiophile speakers, of course, but they sound much better than some of the other outdoor speakers I've heard, and better than any other outdoor speaker I auditioned in this price range.
-They're rugged, which you really need in an outdoor speaker. It's not just rain, after all; an outdoor speaker has to contend with errant footballs, rough handling, curious animals, etc, any of which would break a normal indoor speaker. These have a metal grill and very sturdy build and should stand up to almost anything.
-I like the mounting system; very flexible and well-engineered.

The Bad (and these are minor)
-Very cramped, awkward space for the binding posts. I use banana plugs because I need a quick, easy way to hook them up (standing on a ladder, fumbling around behind the speaker) and there's not enough room back there for normal banana plugs. I wound up buying some right-angle plugs (I got the Monoprice), and those resolved this for me.
-Sound quality is good for an outdoor speaker in this price range but if you don't need a rugged speaker, you can get much better sound for the price. As I'm writing this review, the ELAC Debut 2.0 B6.2 is on sale for about the same price as these Atriums, and the ELAC has much better sound. Of course, the ELAC probably wouldn't survive a night on my patio.

Bottom line: If you need an outdoor speaker in this price range, this speaker would be my recommendation.
text_fidelity_b: Polk Audio Atrium 6 Outdoor Speakers with Bass Reflex Enclosure (Pair, Black) - All-Weather Durability | Broad Sound Coverage | Speed-Lock Mounting System

text_fidelity_a:
SABRENT USB 2.0 to DB25 IEEE 1284 Parallel Printer Cable Adapter [HEXNUT Connectors] (CB-1284) Although every new printer has a USB port, I have a few older, but still perfectly functioning printers that only have parallel inputs. I've been using those printers with PCs that have a parallel output port but, as those PCs get retired, it's getting harder to find a way to hook up the old printers. This solves that problem very well.

It's a simple cable. One end is a USB plug; the other is a DB25 female parallel port. IMPORTANT: you want to check your printer to make sure it can accept a DB25 female plug. Many printers only have a 36-pin Centronics input. If so, you need to get this one: [[ASIN:B00IDU0T1Y Sabrent USB to Parallel IEEE 1284 Printer Cable Adapter (CB-CN36)]]

The cable itself is decent. Thin, but the jacket feels more than sturdy enough for the job at hand. It's only 6 foot long which is OK for my needs but just barely. A longer version (10 or 12 foot) would be nice.

Works fine, and no complaints.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: SABRENT USB 2.0 to DB25 IEEE 1284 Parallel Printer Cable Adapter [HEXNUT Connectors] (CB-1284)

text_fidelity_a:
Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100 It takes some getting used to. I have three of these Anker ergos. Two are wireless and are in use at work. One is wired and on my gaming rig at home.

Gaming: My normal mouse is a Logitech gaming mouse which had been my go to for many years. It was fast accurate and had plenty of built in controls for everything I needed. This mouse also has all of the relevant controls and the resolution button is less likely to get accidentally hit than on the Logitech. It does still get hit here and there though. I also find that the vertical style while more comfortable is not as ideal for gaming but honestly speaking is a small niggle in that the comfort is far more appreciated than the slightly awkward hand position (as movements need to be very fast). Is this up to par with other premium gaming controllers? I have my doubts, but it is certainly comfortable and as a wired controller is adequate for sure.

Everyday: Just yes. Especially considering the value. It is both affordable as an ergonomic mouse and comfortable. You may need to make adjustments to your seating angle as the tendency is for this mouse to be most comfortable when your forearm is almost flat on the desk surface.

Look and feel: It is not an especially heavy mouse. But it does have a level of refinement expected on something more costly. It is also well designed and not obscenely gaudy like a lot of products these days. The rubbery matte surface is pleasant and tactile and the buttons are responsive and easy to actuate. The mouse is somewhat full-sized. I don't want to say large because I have small-medium hands and I can use this just fine, but by no means do I have small hands. Those who have small hands might find this more of a challenge to use though I don't doubt you'll get used to it. The primary buttons and grip would be fine, but the locations of the scroll wheel and the forward nav button are a bit of a reach.

Like I said I have three of these in various formats and love them all. Other than my ultra compact travel mouse, these are used on all of my home and work devices. At such a reasonable cost you can't lose by at least trying it.
text_fidelity_b: Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100

text_fidelity_a:
Cisco-Linksys E4200 Dual-Band Wireless-N Router,Black I bought the Cisco E4200 and the Asus RT-N56U. The RT-N56U was better than the E4200 in strength and speed. Transferring files from laptop to NAS server was much faster with the ASUS both wired and wireless. I however decided to stay with the Cisco because the attached USB hard drive (NTFS) works flawlessly with Windows Backup (not the case with the RT-N56U).

Anyhow, I just switched to AT&T U-verse and tried to have the E4200 get an internet IP address automatically. For some reason it didn't. The ASUS here performed great, as soon as I plugged the cable from AT&T modem/router it configured itself. Amazing! Again... I need those backups in NTFS drives, otherwise I would stick with the RT-N56U.

After trying to troubleshoot myself and losing connection with their chat support, I had to call tech support (in India or surrounding areas). I spent almost hour and a half on the phone, resetting and rebooting everything. The router would just not get an internet IP address. They suggested that the router may be defective, but that I should call AT&T and see if there was something they could do on their end???

Instead of doing that, I drove to my sister house and got her E4200(I did the same setup in her house the week before and it worked well). When I plugged it in, it got the internet IP address immediately, no problems at all.

Both routers had the exact same firmware and settings which indicated to me that the problem was most likely with my E4200.

Again to call Cisco tech support. I explained what happened and told the tech that I had disconnected the router, and that I wanted a replacement. After many questions about how many PCs and laptops I had in my house -irrelevant to the case-, he asked me if there was a cable in lan port one, I replied NO, then he asked the same question about port 2, I replied NO, and so on, until he asked me if there was power going to the router, to which I obviously reply NO. So he said sarcastically 'how do you expect the router to work if it is disconnected?'. I replied 'what part of "I disconnected the router" you did not understand. Misunderstandings like this happened with all the technicians I spoke to.

Another one told me that I had voided my warranty for upgrading the firmware in the router. She scolded me for doing so stating that 3rd party firmware can have bricked the router. I explained to her that I downloaded the firmware from the Cisco support website. She kept going on. I am still trying to figure out where she got the idea that I got 3rd party firmware. What a show of ignorance!

When I asked for a supervisor, they put me on hold for 28 min. After that I was told that there was nobody available. Then the call got mysteriously disconnected when I asked the tech for his full name and badge number.

It is not only Cisco, I know. Many companies do it this way. But it is upsetting that Cisco can not source people who understand and speak English well enough to have a professional conversation. Based on this experience I wonder if these Cisco 'technicians' hold at least a high school diploma.
Yeah, they offer support 24-7-365, but it is not real support if they can not help you or even understand you.

My final advice, if you go for it, test the every single feature of the router. If you find any flaw, deal with Amazon, exchange it or get a refund. Do not try to deal with Cisco-Linksys. It is not worth the aggravation.
text_fidelity_b: Cisco-Linksys E4200 Dual-Band Wireless-N Router,Black

text_fidelity_a:
SAMSUNG (MB-ME32GA/AM) 32GB 95MB/s (U1) microSDHC EVO Select Memory Card with Full-Size Adapter So far so good on this micro sD card.

This is the third micro sD card I’ve bought for my phones since October 2015.

The other two were the 32GB EVO Class 10 Micro SDHC up to 48MB/s with Adapter (MB-MP32DA/AM). And, I was definitely elated to see those were no longer available. Sorry that it is mean-spirited, but after knowing why – I think anyone would be happy to see a fault product go away.

Why did I choose this one?

I purchased the 32GB EVO Class 10 Micro SDHC up to 48MB/s with Adapter (MB-MP32DA/AM) in October of 2015 for my Samsung GS4, and only two (2) months later – I needed a brand new one. Why? It failed. No warning, nothing. Just a failure. The phone wasn’t dropped, shocked, or smashed. It had NO water damage either.

And this wouldn’t be the first failure either for that particular model.

The sD card I bought in December failed as well, but I’ll give it up for it – It went OVER three (3) years before failing. It failed April 3, 2019. I remember that because of the event it failed during. I would’ve expected the failure when I transferred the sD card from the S4 to the S8 in May 2018, but the card still worked.

There were no signs of pending failure or issues. The night before (4/2), it worked and I was able to retrieve some photos off of it.

My mother and I went to Knott’s Berry Farm for the Boysenberry Festival. And, any photos take before we left – GONE. No error messages – just gone. I didn’t know until I got home.

What photos I have were the return photos from the drive home. I had briefly glanced at the card data (on my phone) at about 2pm, but after that (without being dropped, banged, over-heated) the card failed. I know some will ask why I didn’t back them up – I was in transit, driving on the freeway, so it wasn’t feasible.

All I know is that my photos were gone. Again, the phone wasn’t dropped, smashed, shocked. Also, no water damage.

So, I had to purchase another sD card for my phone. This time I chose this one – Samsung 32GB 95MB/s (U1) MicroSD EVO Select Memory Card with Adapter (MB-ME32GA/AM).

From April 2019 to the date of this review, it’s been pretty solid. Though I’m not taking any chances. I also store photos to my S8’s internal storage as well as the sD card.

As far as recommending this one – so far it’s working and has been for over five (5) months, so I’ll recommend it for now.

I’ll update the review if things change.
text_fidelity_b: SAMSUNG (MB-ME32GA/AM) 32GB 95MB/s (U1) microSDHC EVO Select Memory Card with Full-Size Adapter

text_fidelity_a:
Blink Whole Home Bundle | Video Doorbell System, Outdoor camera, and Mini camera | HD video, motion detection, Works with Alexa "Set up in minutes"?? Not really. There are no actual detailed instructions included. I tried scanning the QR code that was provided in the little pamphlet, and that was not helpful. This ended up being extremely frustrating to set up. I could take a wild guess that I was supposed put the lithium batteries in the back of the camera. I would not have known that the little QR code inside the camera where the batteries go was something that I had to scan to set up the camera. Anyway, without going into detail, if Amazon provided some simple, basic instructions with photos that show step by step, it would save the customer a ton of fumbling around. Then it might have been an easy set up. I had to call for support, and by the time I got a support person on the phone I was pretty irritated. The reason I decided to buy this camera is the "two-year battery life." Note: these are not rechargeable batteries. We'll see how long the batteries last. Prior to this, I got a Eufy Solocam, also wireless (and much, much easier to set up), and it had rechargeable batteries advertised to last 4 months, but they lasted 4 weeks. A feature that is missing with the Blink camera, that I liked on the Eufy camera, is the AI feature to recognize humans. Without the AI feature, the Blink is recording non-human motion, such as animals and vehicles.

Update: The description advertises customized zones for motion detection. The camera takes a photo what it sees, and in motion settings, you gray out areas that you do not want the camera to detect motion. It does NOT work. I tried resetting it several times, and the camera recorded and sent me an alert of motion detected that was squarely in the grayed out area. Without this feature actually working, and without the AI feature to detect humans, the camera is recording every motion in the entire viewable area, ignoring the areas that I grayed out. I am returning this camera.
text_fidelity_b: Blink Whole Home Bundle | Video Doorbell System, Outdoor camera, and Mini camera | HD video, motion detection, Works with Alexa

text_fidelity_a:
Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) I have been using the Kindle for exactly one week and it has exceeded my expectations in every way except for one design flaw.

Downloading books is absolutely a breeze and the selection of titles (for a premier launch of a product) is simply outstanding. I cannot wait to see what else will be added in the future and my credit card is ready and waiting.

Figuring out how to use the Kindle was easier than figuring out my basic LG cellphone. I am, obviously, a technical loser, but the Kindle has made me feel like a genius. And the instruction manual makes everything logical and simple to do - layed out for the quickest access. You don't feel intimidated or stupid when attempting to look something up.

My only complaint is that I wish there were some way of locking the right side "turn page" function. Unfortunately I have had to learn to grab my Kindle from the top and bottom because if I handle it from the sides, I will end up rapidly changing pages. And I know better than to lean it against anything on the right or left side for the same reason.

This the best Christmas gift I could have hoped for. I am now in the process of reading 6 different books, with 2 more in the queue. Not to mention 3 blogs which I check throughout the day.

The Kindle has opened up new worlds for me and is giving me the opportunity to discover subjects that I would never have considered in a million years. And why not? Instead of stacking books throughout my house, I can now carry them around in a compact unit which is lighter than a paperback.

I don't know who to thank for this wonderful creation, but I can assure you that I will be a customer for life.
text_fidelity_b: Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th)

It used to be a 10 out of 10 but I’m down to about 3 out of 10. But that high whine every night absolutely precludes good sleep.

I was so excited to get this product. The set up was easy and I fell asleep right away… But about 3 hours later I awoke to electronic blow back noises. Thank God.

Cervical tinnitus vs. hearing loss or ear damage tinnitus works in different ways … and I am certain this product works for many people…I am just posting my individual experience. I’m returning it and I pulled the trigger for the $99 pillow speaker which is the size of an iPad which is placed between your pillowcase and your pillow.

ASUS AC3100 WiFi Router (RT-AC3100) - Dual Band Wireless Internet Router, Trend Micro Lifetime AiProtection, AiMesh Compatible, Parental Control, MU-MIMO ASUS makes excellent routers overall with the added bonus of being compatible with a variety of free-ware router software like DD-WRT, Tomato, and Merlin-WRT (recommended). It includes all of the features you need for a proper home LAN, far better than the junky wireless routers offered by your internet provider, especially Comcast XFinity. (Don't believe the hype- their equipment is terrible.)

Some great features include
- Great 802.11ac support (5 GHz wireless support)
- Legacy 802.11b support (2.4 Ghz wireless support used in most cheap IOT devices)
- DHCP support which includes local DNS and MAC ID binding to make NAT and Firewall rules effective with having to manually configure your devices with easy to use client management
- Easy to use QOS with instrumentation features
- VPN support
- Many storage solution variants to allow for of personal cloud and LAN network storage (NAS-like functionality)
- Gaming networking enhancements galore
- Excellent security features
- Excellent compatibility with other devices
- Excellent and easy to use web-base administration software
- Excellent community support on countless on-line forums
- Best router for the money; Similarly featured Netgear routers are significantly more expensive without a real edge

Some downsides:
- Terrible vendor support (not really necessary unless you need a warranty replacement, but they are okay here)
- Some software limitations make many features will only work when you use local subnets within the 192.168.0.0/16 class B network
- Network storage throughput somewhat slow

It is devices like this that have had me a loyal ASUS customer for routers for nearly a decade. The fact that you can use Merlin-WRT as your software which IMHO more stable than the factory firmware makes it a slam-dunk.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS AC3100 WiFi Router (RT-AC3100) - Dual Band Wireless Internet Router, Trend Micro Lifetime AiProtection, AiMesh Compatible, Parental Control, MU-MIMO

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Sense 2 Advanced Health and Fitness Smartwatch with Tools to Manage Stress and Sleep, ECG App, SpO2, 24/7 Heart Rate and GPS, Shadow Grey/Graphite, One Size (S & L Bands Included) At this point, I have had the Sense 2 for 2 days and I know at least some of my issues will likely be fixed with later software updates. First, the good. I like the form factor. The case is thin and the watch, even with the supplied band, is comfortable. Speaking of the band, as a big guy, I was overjoyed to see the inclusion of a second band that actually fit. Also, changing bands is a snap.

Overall, it seems to be relatively high quality. The battery life, so far at least has been fantastic. I am on hour 42 of wearing it after a 99% charge and it is down to 70% battery left. The screen is fairly bright and crisp. An understated advantage of the Sense 2 (and one of the reasons I switched) is that is OS and phone brand agnostic. You can use it with Apple or Android and, unlike the Galaxy Watch, there are no features locked away if you are not using the correct brand of phone.

If you are coming from a Galaxy Watch where you could customize the watch face and all sorts of other things and that is important to you, then move along. This watch will not be for you. For now, at least, there is not really much substantive you can do to individualize your user experience. That's not so great.

Also not so great is the things that are missing. There is no Google Maps at launch. Also, despite being a Google company, no support for the Google Assistant (Alexa only sadly). There is also no interface to control music on your phone if that is important to you. I found it mildly annoying, but not a deal breaker. In addition, some people will be turned off by the fact that there are features that require a Fitbit paid subscription to get, even though you get six months for free.

The real reason I bought this watch was the ECG function. I have had A Fib for a couple of years and used to use (and still do) a Kardia XL to check my rhythm. The Galaxy Watch 4 was nice because it did a reasonable single lead reading and it meant not having to carry another gizmo with me. You simply held still and put a finger on each of the side buttons. Unfortunately, when I switched from a Galaxy phone to a Pixel, I lost the ability to do an ECG.

On the Sense 2, the ECG has not been impressive. First, I have big hands and contorting my right one to get my thumb and forefinger on the corner of the glass has been a challenge at time. It often takes several tries to get it right. Second, despite confirming on both my Kardia and my Galaxy Watch, the Sense 2 will never indicate that I am in A Fib. Apparently, if your pulse goes above 120 (which mine frequently does while in A Fib) then the Sense 2 just gives up and won't really check. Even in instances where it was below 120, the Sense will not confirm. I guess we get to settle for inconclusive results instead. Given this feature was the main reason I bought the watch, it may be a deal breaker for me and I may return it for that reason. If this feature is not that important to you, then it may still be a good option.

Overall though, it may be a good option for the right person. If you care primarily about health and fitness tracking and want a good battery life, then this is a good option. At the current $300 price point, I still feel like Fitbit may be asking a little too much given the features of the other higher end options on the market.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Sense 2 Advanced Health and Fitness Smartwatch with Tools to Manage Stress and Sleep, ECG App, SpO2, 24/7 Heart Rate and GPS, Shadow Grey/Graphite, One Size (S & L Bands Included)

Sennheiser Momentum 3 Wireless - Active Noise Cancelling Headphones with Alexa, Auto On/Off, Smart Pause Functionality and Smart Control App - White The sound quality on these is excellent across the board:
*high definition: you will hear every detail from breathing and clothing moving, to the sound of a violin stroke changing direction in the orchestra
*powerful bass: listening to a deep beat is excellent with these
*crisp treble: not tinny, just crisp and clear

The smart pause stops your music when you take the headphones off, so interruptions don’t make you lose your place, whether for podcasts or music.

Pairing was easy, and there are lots of controls on the headphones so you can use them for calls, Siri, dictation, etc..

USB-C: these headphones are compatible with my new MacBook pro, but if you do not have anything with USB-C, this includes an adapter for USB-C to standard USB. The last thing one wants to do is drop more money just to charge these, so it’s good they included this to make it portable and usable.

Speaking of portability, the carry case is soft, which means it won’t protect the headphones well. This looked cheaper than I expected, especially considering that I own significantly cheaper headphones than these with a better case. It might seem petty to point this out, but part of having noise cancelling headphones is usually because you travel and want to block the noise of an airplane, train, or ship engine out. If the case isn’t good for travel, then it’s a problem, and you have to figure out another way to pack these, whether that means buying something that is not a great fit for the size, or just risking it.
text_fidelity_b: Sennheiser Momentum 3 Wireless - Active Noise Cancelling Headphones with Alexa, Auto On/Off, Smart Pause Functionality and Smart Control App - White
